chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Ayman ibn Muhraz, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) married off a woman from the Banu Abd al-Muttalib, and he was in charge of her matter, so he said: 'All praise is for Allah, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Lenient, the Forgiver, the One, the Subduer, the Great, the Exalted. It is the same from you all, whether you speak secretly or publicly, whether you are concealed by night or visible by day. I testify that there is no god but Allah, One, with no partner, to whom belongs the Kingdom and the Praise, and He is Able over all things. And I testify that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is His servant and His Messenger, whom He sent with His Book as a proof upon His servants. Whoever obeys him obeys Allah, and whoever disobeys him disobeys Allah. May Allah bless him and his family abundantly. The Imam of Guidance and the Chosen Prophet. Then I advise you with the fear of Allah, for it is Allah's advice in the past and the bygone days.' Then he solemnized the marriage.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Title of Imam Ali)
key_terms.بَنِي عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ: The Clan of Abd al-Muttalib (Prophetic lineage)

ai.seo_question: What was the sermon delivered by Imam Ali during the marriage ceremony of a woman from Banu Abd al-Muttalib?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* records the marriage sermon of Imam Ali (AS), highlighting the theological principle that God’s omniscience renders the distinction between secret and public deeds irrelevant, a concept rooted in Surah Ibrahim. The sermon underscores the inseparable link between prophetic obedience and divine will, serving as a foundational text for Shia jurisprudence regarding marital rites and the spiritual authority of the Imams. It concludes with a universal exhortation to *taqwa*, framing it as the enduring covenant of all prophets.
